# Requirements Document: Matching a photoid to a boarding pass

## Introduction

For contactless travel a touchpoint needs a boarding pass together with the
face image of a photoid (§4.1.2), and the guide assumes the holder of the
wallet is a passenger (§3.2).  The guide gives no rule for deciding that a
photoid and a boarding pass presented together are about the same traveler.
This module keeps the readings of what a relying party could check from the
two credentials alone.  A reading that uses the device key is added with the
presentation flows.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneId/Traveler.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/verified-id/blob/main/Rules/OneId/Traveler.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet. *Sources* lists the sections of the guide each rule was written from, *External specifications* lists the specifications it relies on and whether this project has read each, and *Confirmation* says whether anyone outside the model has confirmed the rule as written.

## Requirements

### Requirement OID-107

**User Story:** As an airport touchpoint, I want the face I match and the boarding pass I admit to belong to one traveler, so that nobody boards on another person's boarding pass.

**Rule:** WHEN a photoid and a boarding pass are presented together THE SYSTEM SHALL accept the pair only if both are about the same traveler. (Lean: `travelerMatch`)

**Sources:** [One ID Technical Implementation Guide 26.3, §4.1.2 Boarding pass](https://standards.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OneID/pages/2947416082/Technical+Implementation+Guide) (standard); [One ID Technical Implementation Guide 26.3, §3.2 Assumption](https://standards.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OneID/pages/2947416082/Technical+Implementation+Guide) (standard); [One ID Technical Implementation Guide 26.3, §1.4 Technical Guidance Scope](https://standards.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OneID/pages/2947416082/Technical+Implementation+Guide) (standard); [Readings of how a photoid and a boarding pass are matched, where the guide states no rule](https://github.com/samdengler/verified-id/blob/main/Rules/OneId/Traveler.lean) (modeller)

**External specifications:** IATA Resolution 792 (BCBP), the resolution as a whole (not read); ISO/IEC TS 23220-4:2026, Annex C, Table C.1 (not read)

**Confirmation:** Not confirmed yet.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. IF a photoid and a boarding pass presented together are about different travelers THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the pair.
   - OID-107.1, open: open theorem `matched_pair_same_traveler`; example `anotherTravelersBoardingPass`; example `twoTravelersWithOneName`
2. WHEN a photoid and a boarding pass presented together are about the same traveler THE SYSTEM SHALL accept the pair.
   - OID-107.2, open: open theorem `same_traveler_matches`; example `ownBoardingPassRefused`

#### Open question on OID-107.1

> A photoid and a boarding pass that the system accepts as a pair are about
> the same traveler.
>
> Open question for the business.  The guide requires a boarding pass together
> with the face image of a photoid at a contactless touchpoint and assumes the
> holder of the wallet is a passenger.  It names no data element to compare and
> no way to compare them.  As written, any accepted photoid goes with any
> accepted boarding pass: the example `anotherTravelersBoardingPass` shows
> one traveler's face admitted on another traveler's boarding pass.  Comparing
> names does not settle it: the example `twoTravelersWithOneName` shows two
> travelers with the same name.  No check of the two credentials' content can
> settle it by itself \(`no_content_check_identifies_the_traveler`\), because
> who a credential is about is fixed at issuance, which the guide puts out of
> scope.  What ties a photoid and a boarding pass to one traveler: a rule for
> issuers, the device key, or something else, and what must a relying party
> check?

#### Open question on OID-107.2

> A photoid and a boarding pass about the same traveler are accepted as a
> pair.
>
> Open question for the business.  If names are compared, the name in a photoid
> comes from the passport and the name in a boarding pass string follows
> Resolution 792, and the guide does not say how to compare the two.  Under an
> exact comparison, a traveler whose passport name has an accent or a second
> given name is refused with their own boarding pass.  The example
> `ownBoardingPassRefused` shows it.  If names are compared, how are a
> passport name and a boarding pass name brought to the same form?
